material.title: Week 1: JavaScript Variables, Constants, and Assignment

sections.heading: Concepts
sections.body: In JavaScript, variables are used to store data values. They can hold different types of information such as numbers, strings, or even other objects. A constant is a variable whose value cannot be changed once it has been set. This means that constants are immutable and their value remains fixed throughout the program's execution. Assignment in JavaScript involves setting a variable to a specific value.

sections.heading: Worked example
Practice
sections.body: Now let's practice what we've learned with a simple task. Write a short JavaScript program that uses variables and constants. Your program should have two variables: one named `firstName` set to your name, and another constant `courseCode` set to the course code from this syllabus outline (`IT 102`). Print both values to the console.

activity.title: Trace Values in a Short JavaScript Program

sections.heading: Part A: Write Your Code
sections.body: Write a short JavaScript program that includes two variables and one constant. One variable should be named `firstName` and set to your name. The other variable should be named `courseCode` and set to the course code from this syllabus outline (`IT 102`). Both values should then be printed to the console.

sections.heading: Part B: Submit Your Code
sections.body: Submit your JavaScript program for review. Ensure that you include both `firstName` and `courseCode` variables, with appropriate assignment statements, and a `console.log()` statement to display their values.
